entries.agent_impact: A consumer may now read a declarative, schema-validated description of how a checkout at a resolved commit becomes a usable installed runtime, and enforce it: exact commands, accepted Node and npm ranges, per-step network policy, the enumerated input set, seven mandatory output checks, and five bounds. It is data only — this repository publishes the recipe and executes no step of it. Enforcement is fail-closed: an unrecognized recipe kind, revision, or safety-critical enum is refused, and a check that cannot be performed counts as failed rather than skipped. Two readings a consumer must not take: the input set is the compiler's resolved file list rather than its configured globs, and campaign-spec/dist is a build output with no committed baseline, so output verification is self-consistency rather than comparison against a hash published here. A prepared generation can build and type-check but cannot run browser QA. Nothing existing changed shape; adoption is optional and additive.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/unknown-kind.json. recipe_kind names a kind this schema version does not define. An installed consumer was not released knowing how to execute it, so it fails closed rather than guessing that a v2 is a v1 with extras.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/unknown-revision.json. recipe_revision leaves the major line the kind defines. A revision may only re-parameterise fields the consumer already understands; a different major is a shape change wearing a revision's clothes.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/unknown-network-policy.json. A safety-critical enum: the install step declares a network policy outside the defined set. There is no allow-all value, and an unrecognized one is refused rather than treated as permissive.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/allowlist-without-hosts.json. An allowlist with no hosts is not a bound, it is an empty declaration that reads like one. The schema requires a non-empty host list whenever the policy is an allowlist.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/unknown-output-check.json. A safety-critical enum: an output check names a kind the consumer cannot perform. A new KIND of check is a new recipe kind, because an installed consumer cannot perform a check it was not released knowing.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/unknown-step-id.json. A safety-critical enum: a step identity outside the defined set. Steps are identified rather than positional, so an unrecognized id is a command the consumer has no contract for.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/lifecycle-scripts-enabled.json. A safety-critical enum: a step that permits lifecycle scripts. Enabling them would let the target run arbitrary code during preparation, which is the single thing the recipe's flags exist to prevent.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/engines-disagreement-warns.json. A safety-critical enum: disagreement between the contract's tool range and the target's declared engines resolved as a warning. An accept-with-warning path produces a build made under conditions nobody approved.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/advisory-enforcement.json. fail_closed switched off. Advisory bounds record the right numbers and enforce nothing, so the first time a bound matters you discover it was decorative.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/unperformable-check-skipped.json. A safety-critical enum: a check that cannot be performed treated as skipped. A skipped check reports success it never established.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/committed-output-claim.json. The recipe claims its output directory is a committed artifact. It is not: the directory is git-ignored and untracked, so no baseline for its contents can exist here and verification must be self-consistency.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/unpinned-lockfile.json. The recipe claims its lockfile is not integrity-pinned. The network allowlist bounds where bytes may come from and the lockfile's digests bound which bytes are acceptable; dropping the second leaves the first standing alone, which it was never meant to do.

A refused runtime-recipe fixture, one mutation of the accepted recipe: reject/missing-required-field.json. The enumerated input set is absent. Without it there is nothing to fingerprint, and staleness — the one failure mode no output-side check can see — becomes undetectable.

entries.agent_impact: A fourth checkpoint gate is registered, built_output.upsell_selector_scope, and it can block a doctor run that previously passed. It fires when a built page whose funnel role is upsell or downsell carries a data-next-bundle-selector that lacks data-next-upsell-context and is in the default swap selection mode: such a selector writes to the shopper's live cart at init, so loading the page charges them for a package at the next checkout without it appearing in that checkout's rendered order summary. Two consequences a consumer must plan for. First, `doctor --built` can now return blocked; it previously only produced warnings, and a consumer treating that mode as advisory will need to read its exit state. Second, all eight certified template families (apollo, apollo-mv-single-step, demeter, olympus, olympus-mv-single-step, olympus-mv-two-step, shop-single-step, shop-three-step) currently ship a display-only selector with neither attribute across 19 upsell offer includes, so a campaign built from any certified family blocks until the templates are repaired upstream in campaign-cart-starter-templates. The remedy is to add data-next-upsell-context to the named selector, or to record a bounded named-human waiver through `campaigns-os checkpoint waive --gate built_output.upsell_selector_scope`. data-next-selection-mode="select" also clears the blocker and reports a warning instead, because the SDK gates every cart write on swap mode.

entries.agent_impact: Two `qa resolve` outputs that could be believed no longer can be. First, `status: ready` now asserts that the derived entry URLs were probed AND resolved; it previously asserted only that they were derived from the packet, so a route set that was 100% dead reported ready with a next command that could not succeed. A consumer reading resolve status must handle two new terminal values: `routes_unresolved` (probed, at least one route dead, `ok: false`, first failing URL named, `qa run` suggestion suppressed) and `ready_unprobed` (routes existed but none produced a response, `ok: true`). Both are additive; the existing three values keep their meaning over probed-and-resolved routes. The status ladder is ordered by verification coverage, so `ready_unprobed` outranks `ready_with_exceptions` — read `checkpoint_gates[]` for warnings rather than inferring them from status. Offline and CI runs need no flag: a transport error degrades to `ready_unprobed` rather than failing, because a 404 is evidence about the deployment while a transport error is evidence about the caller network. `--no-probe` is for hermetic runs that must make no outbound request. Second, `theme_gate.no_commerce_pages` no longer fires on a campaign whose declared funnel includes commerce pages that this build left out of scope, so a consumer that treated that code as proof of a content-only campaign was reading a build-scope artifact. Theme gate results gain `commerce_pages_out_of_scope`, and `scope_source` gains `doctor_derived_scope+spec_topologies`. Resolve remains a diagnostic command and still exits 0 on every status.
entries.migration: none

entries.agent_impact: Browser QA now emits assertions for two things it previously said nothing about, and both can newly block a verdict that used to pass. A checkout page whose CampaignSpec declares exit_intent or promo_code_input with enabled: true gets browser-exit-intent-surface:<page> / browser-promo-code-surface:<page>: absent markup is FAIL/BLOCKER, markup carrying the declared offer_code is PASS, markup that cannot be tied to that code (or a coupon input behind an unopened disclosure) is MANUAL_REVIEW/WARN, and a browser collector that threw mid-read is SKIPPED with the cause rather than blocking. Typed-card runs additionally emit browser-order-display-parity:<plan> and browser-order-total-parity:<plan>, reconciling the persisted order pre-upsell read-back against what the checkout displayed at submit; a non-upsell line whose package was never rendered as selected, a displayed package that was never charged, or a total that disagrees with the displayed summary total is FAIL/BLOCKER naming the package ids. Both reconciliation assertions report SKIPPED with a stated reason when the page gives them nothing comparable - a summary whose rows do not all carry data-package-id, or a checkout with no [data-next-display="cart.total"] surface - and a consumer must read that as missing coverage, never as a pass. Both sets reuse the existing browser-runtime and browser-test-order families, so the verdict schema, QA_ASSERTION_FAMILY_VOCABULARY, and any allowlist keyed off it are unchanged. A campaign that declares a surface it did not build, or charges a package it never displayed, will now block where it previously reported ready.

Which dispositions end a session is one exported set, SESSION_ENDING_DISPOSITIONS, read by both the auto-end and the closeout it prints; membership is enumerated rather than excluded, so a disposition from a newer or foreign verdict keeps the session open on both sides instead of leaving them to disagree over who owns the run_id.

It says browser QA will block on the starter palette and names the two lanes that clear it: `campaigns-os theme waive` (downgrades those rows to warn severity) or a hand-authored brand-theme.css loaded after next-core.css. A family outside the certified set (custom, undecided, or any family with no contract) produces no palette rows, so it is not warned. The non-JSON tiny prompt prints the same warning alongside, not instead of, the stage's existing prompt. No gate status, severity, or exit code changes, and nothing is waived automatically; a waived or applied gate emits nothing. A second non-required action, theme_gate.brand_contract_unreadable, appears at the same stages when the family's brand contract exists but fails to load (parse_error, schema_mismatch, extends_cycle, extends_missing_parent, family_mismatch): it names the family and the error code and says browser QA rejects such a contract outright as a template-brand-contract:<family> blocker that no waiver clears. That one does not depend on the theme gate outcome, because QA rejects the contract whether or not the campaign has brand tokens; a family that simply resolves to no contract is not a defect and emits nothing. next still never throws over a defective contract. Every value interpolated into that advisory is bounded before it is printed or serialized: the family must match the lowercase template-family slug or it reads unknown-family, the code must be one of the loader's own or it reads unknown, and the loader detail is folded to one trimmed line with control characters stripped, Markdown escaped, and length capped; the repair path names contracts/template-brand-contract.<family>.v0.json only when that file is on disk and otherwise names the private fragment supplying it. A consumer that treats every next_actions[] entry as a command to execute must read `command: null` / absent `required` as advisory, as it already must for purchase_proof_unknown and run_record_present.

entries.agent_impact: QA and doctor findings now carry a cause class, so a consumer can tell whether the change under test caused what a run surfaced instead of re-reading every finding by hand. Two additive optional fields ride each finding: cause (caused_by_change | pre_existing | test_environment | upstream_drift | unknown) and cause_reason (a short reason code). A cause_summary object ({surface, total, counts, prior_run_id, comparison}, plus prior_qa_attempt_run_id on the QA side) rides the QA verdict and the doctor output; prior_run_id is the previous Run Record's id on both surfaces, and the QA summary additionally names the final attempt within that record it read. The fields appear on the full verdict, on the derived exceptions, on the committed QA verdict sidecar, and on every doctor result — classification is applied where the doctor result is produced, so all four producers that persist .campaign-runtime/doctor-output.json leave the labels on the retained artifact. Passing assertions carry none, and non-packet doctor (--built / --site) is not annotated. Absence is not a claim: output emitted before this release carries neither field, and the first run on a campaign labels every finding unknown because there is no earlier run to compare against. The human reports gained a summary line and a per-finding tag; the doctor issue line keeps its existing "[code] message" shape with the tag appended.

A consumer that wants the labels to be meaningful must let campaigns-os run-record write a Run Record after each run, since the previous run is found through Run Record discovery.

entries.agent_impact: Four documented facts a consumer may have been getting wrong, with no behaviour change behind them. First, a checkpoint gate's status is the blocking axis only: page_kit.store_profile returns status pass with code page_kit.store_profile.target_only and the affected fields in warning_fields[] when the target declares a governed Store Profile field the CampaignSpec leaves empty, and qa resolve chooses between ready and ready_with_exceptions from warning_fields[] (or an active waiver), not from status — so read code and warning_fields[], never status alone, to decide whether a gate is clean. Second, sequence is the authoritative order of contracts/release-ledger.json (it is the entry's position in entries[], and the gate derives the expected value from that position) while id is an immutable label that is never reused or renumbered; the two diverge legitimately when concurrent pull requests restamp sequence on merge, so order by sequence and identify by id and infer neither from the other. Third, a change that lives entirely in policy-ignored paths carries a same-surface CHANGELOG section and no ledger entry, because every change item must map to a classified changed path in the range; any src/cli.mjs change is cli_surface and owes an entry. Fourth, Design Source Package intake only reads under the source root and writes every artifact under the target repository, and a screenshots[] record is available with a url as well as a path, so the readiness gate can clear against a source root the operator cannot write and with no capture bytes in the source tree; the manifest path is fixed and source_html.root is stored relative to the packet, so a packet resolves its source from where it was written.

entries.agent_impact: Credential-bearing requests on the telemetry rails now validate before any socket opens, so two silent behaviours change for an agent. An agent that pointed a remit or publish at a plain-http remote proxy will see it fail: on the remit rail non-fatally, with the reason in remit_error / remit_ok false; on telemetry list as a non-zero exit. Spec retrieval by --map-id carries no credential and is unaffected. (2) A campaign key that is present but malformed is now reported as refused rather than missing. resolveCampaignsApiKeySource() returns { key, origin, rejected } and describeCampaignKeyRejection() renders a sentence naming the refused SOURCE (env:VAR, the packet field, or the CampaignSpec) and never the value. telemetry list --packet exits non-zero on such a value and makes no request; run-record warns on stderr and its human summary now says the declared key was refused on shape instead of 'no Campaigns API key found', then attempts the send without a tenant scope (the remit rail stays non-fatal); with no send attempted (consent off, or --no-remit) the key is not read and nothing is said about it. entries.agent_impact: Two surface moves in one version. The standardization-report command is removed: it was a second spelling of standardize with identical flags, output and exit codes, and an agent or script still spelling it now gets the unknown-command error pointing at campaigns-os --help. Use standardize; its flags (--target, --family, --slug, --sdk-support-policy, --field-contract, --no-doctor, --json), its output, and the report's own campaign-standardization-report/v0 schema_version are unchanged. Newly available: the ./text-safety package export publishes singleLineField(value, fallback) and singleLineDetail(detail, max), the flatteners the CLI uses before printing a value it did not author, so a consumer rendering a run id, a target path or a quoted loader message into its own single-line notice can apply the same escape set instead of reimplementing it. singleLineField replaces C0, DEL and C1 with U+FFFD without dropping characters; singleLineDetail additionally turns line breaks into spaces, collapses whitespace, backslash-escapes Markdown, and truncates to max (default 300) with an ellipsis, reporting (no detail reported) for an empty value. Both moved to src/text-safety.mjs with no behaviour change.
entries.migration: Replace campaigns-os standardization-report with campaigns-os standardize; every flag, the output and the exit codes are identical, so nothing else changes. A consumer pinning cli_commands drops standardization-report from its pinned list, and may add the ./text-safety package export.

entries.agent_impact: Behaviour change in campaigns-os qa run --test-order for one page shape only. The runner's cart-entry control set no longer includes [data-next-checkout-action="add-to-cart"] or [data-next-add-to-cart]; it is exactly the SDK's activation selector, [data-next-action="add-to-cart"]. A landing page whose only add-to-cart control uses one of the two removed spellings now fails the entered_via_landing step immediately with cart_entry_control_missing (order_creation classification not_created, no reservation, no click) instead of clicking the control and failing with cart_entry_no_navigation after the navigation budget. The primary-CTA assertion on such a page no longer credits the element's data-next-url as a route, so a page with no other route CTA reports missing_route_cta. Pages with the SDK's own control or a ?forcePackageId= checkout link behave exactly as before. Verdict field names and codes are unchanged; only which code such a page receives, and how quickly, changes.
entries.migration: None for a page the SDK actually wires. entries.agent_impact: Additive. The ./text-safety package export gains singleLineFragment(value, fallback): line breaks and tabs become spaces, runs of whitespace collapse, the ends are trimmed, every other control character (C0 other than whitespace, DEL, C1) becomes U+FFFD, no Markdown escaping, no length cap; an empty or absent value returns fallback (default the empty string). Use it for a toolkit-derived value folded into a sentence, such as a gate's required_actions[].command or .description. singleLineField and singleLineDetail keep their signatures and their exact output; singleLineDetail is now defined as singleLineFragment plus Markdown escaping, the cap and the (no detail reported) placeholder. One stderr line changes on hostile input only: the qa run browser-skipped notice's quoted required actions now render a non-whitespace control character as U+FFFD instead of a space. No JSON output changes.
entries.migration: None. A consumer that reimplemented the sentence fold can import singleLineFragment instead.

changes.summary: The ./text-safety row names singleLineFragment beside singleLineField and singleLineDetail, states which value kind each is for (own field, folded into a sentence, quoted detail) and what each does to whitespace and to other control characters, and records that singleLineFragment was added at 1.27.0+agent.2.

entries.agent_impact: Internal consolidation with one narrow behaviour change. The helpers that read a campaign's route identity (public_route_slug and route_root) moved from private copies in src/cli.mjs, src/qa-node.mjs, src/source-html-intake.mjs and src/page-kit-campaign-config.mjs into one leaf, src/route-identity.mjs; no command's flags, exit codes, doctor JSON or doctor text change. What changes: qa run now reads a packet's campaign.route_root by the same exact rule doctor does (exactly "/" or exactly "/<public_route_slug>/"). A packet whose route_root is any other spelling of the slug ("/<slug>" without the trailing slash, "<slug>/", "//<slug>//", a case mismatch) was already a doctor blocker (campaign.route_root) and is now treated by QA as an ignored declaration too: QA audits the slug-prefixed default "/<slug>/", which is the root it used for that packet before as well, so the pages QA visits do not change and no verdict field changes. A CampaignSpec's route_root keeps the lenient intake reading prepare-build canonicalises. An agent that compares doctor and QA outcomes on a packet no longer sees the two disagree about a mistyped route_root.
entries.migration: None. A packet already accepted by doctor is unaffected; a packet doctor blocks on campaign.route_root should have that value corrected to exactly "/" or "/<public_route_slug>/", which was already the documented rule.

changes.summary: campaignRouteRoot, isAbsoluteHttpUrl, normalizePublicRouteSlug, stripPublicRoutePrefix and runtimeRelativeRouteForSpecValue are imported from src/route-identity.mjs instead of being defined in cli.mjs; validateRouteRootDeclaration decides acceptance through the leaf's packetRouteRoot, the same rule the QA runner now reads the packet by. Doctor's issue codes, ready lines, JSON and text output are unchanged.
The route_root rule states that qa run reads the packet by doctor's rule, so a value doctor blocks never roots a QA check and a hand-edited packet cannot pass QA at a root doctor refuses.

entries.agent_impact: Two behaviour changes, both only for a packet kept outside its target repo (prepare-build --out) or whose Assembly Report is not the default sidecar (prepare-build --report-out); a packet at its target root with the default report sees no change. (1) campaigns-os doctor now writes .campaign-runtime/doctor-output.json under the target repo (packet.assembly.target_repo resolved against the packet's directory) instead of beside the packet, which is where prepare-build, next and the QA stage refresh already wrote it and where theme waive / qa policy set apply their stale stamp. An agent that read the doctor sidecar beside a packet kept elsewhere must read it under the target repo; --doctor-out still overrides. (2) qa run and qa waive read, and the QA stage record after qa run writes, the Assembly Report the Build Context binds (its report_path, relative to the target repo) instead of the default sidecar; for a --report-out campaign the QA stage now lands in the report next reads, where before it was silently dropped. The runner's own reads of doctor-output.json, build-context.json and the Assembly Report (theme gate, polish gate, recorded QA waivers) resolve the same way, so they see what doctor and next wrote. A Build Context binds a report only for the packet its packet_path names; one naming another packet is not followed (the default report is used, as before). --report still overrides on every command. Doctor JSON and text output, verdict fields and exit codes are unchanged.
entries.migration: None for a packet at its target root. For a packet kept elsewhere, read doctor-output.json under the target repo (or pass --doctor-out); a stale copy beside the packet from earlier doctor runs can be deleted. For a --report-out campaign, re-run qa run to record the QA stage into the bound report.

entries.agent_impact: Three things change for an agent. (1) doctor gains a warning code, campaign.api_key_rejected: a Campaigns API key that is present but refused on shape (not 8-256 chars of letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore, one line), or an api_key_source env var whose name does not name a campaign key, is reported under it with detail { source, kind } (kind malformed or unsupported_env_name), where doctor previously reported such a value as available (ready line 'Campaigns API key available via ...'). A key that is simply not configured is unchanged under campaign.api_key_source. (2) One ready-line wording follows the shared resolver: a key sourced from the CampaignSpec reads 'Campaigns API key available via the packet-local CampaignSpec campaign.campaigns_api_key' (previously 'via CampaignSpec campaign.campaigns_api_key'); packet and env sources read as before. (3) On the remit rails (run-record remit, QA verdict publish, telemetry list --packet), api_key_source env:CAMPAIGNS_API_KEY and env:CAMPAIGN_KEY are now accepted; since 1.26.0+agent.22 they were refused by name because the env-name rule anchored the first letter before looking for CAMPAIGN. Names containing CAMPAIGN after other characters were, and are, accepted; foreign names are still refused.
